Squads:

West Indies head into the series on the back of a convincing Test series win over Sri Lanka just a month ago and will look to build on that momentum in familiar conditions. Pakistan, meanwhile, begin another phase with Babar Azam back at the helm, hoping the leadership change can bring better results after a difficult period in red-ball cricket. With valuable World Test Championship points up for grabs, neither side can afford a slow start.

There is also plenty of interest around how this surface behaves over the next five days, with the slower bowlers expected to have a role as the match progresses. The forecast carries a slight chance of rain throughout the Test, including from the second session today. Let's hope the weather stays away and allows for an uninterrupted contest. Toss and team news coming up shortly, stay tuned...

11:15 local, 15:15 GMT, 20:45 IST: Rain stops play, but it doesn't look too worrying. The eastern skies are clear, and if the weather behaves as expected, this should only be a short delay. Fingers crossed we are back underway soon.

11:40 local, 15:40 GMT, 21:10 IST: Still no respite from the weather. The rain continues to fall heavily and shows little sign of easing. With just 20 minutes left before the scheduled lunch break, the chances of getting any more play in this session are beginning to look increasingly slim.
